Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Bill 2013 - Consideration in Detail - Agree to the bill
Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Share mining boom benefits
Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Read a second time

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved a debate management motion capping the Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Bill's second reading debate and limiting consideration in detail to 60 minutes, defending it as routine scheduling and noting the House was waiting to hear the member for Banks give his maiden speech.

speeches.speaker: Chris Bowen
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill repealing the mining tax and other measures, comparing it to opposition raised against the Hawke government's petroleum resource rent tax, which has since raised $39 billion, and criticised the retrospective abolition of the low income superannuation contribution for people earning under $37,000 while high-income superannuation tax breaks remain.

speeches.speaker: Jenny Macklin
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill's abolition of the schoolkids bonus, the income support bonus and the low income superannuation contribution, saying 1.3 million families and 2.2 million children would be worse off, and that families could lose up to $15,000 over their children's schooling.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Defended the profits-based mining tax, citing Treasury's own costings showing its repeal would cost the budget around $4 billion, noted mining exploration spending rose from $5.7 billion in 2009-10 to $7.8 billion in 2012-13 despite the tax, and quoted evidence that Fortescue Metals Group had not yet paid any corporate tax.

speeches.speaker: Luke Simpkins
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the mining tax as a clear election commitment, argued mining resources belong to the states rather than the Commonwealth, and accused the former Labor government of fostering entitlement, recalling that Kevin Rudd's 2007 election promise of a Western Australian infrastructure fund was never delivered.

speeches.speaker: Luke Simpkins
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the mining tax, noting it raised only about $400 million against $16.7 billion in committed spending over the forward estimates, and said Australia has gone from $60 billion in surplus in 2007 to $292 billion in debt, criticising the schoolkids bonus payments of $800 and $400 as an unfunded handout.

speeches.speaker: Nick Champion
speeches.brief: Opposed the mining tax repeal bill, warning it scraps the low-income superannuation contribution of up to $500 for workers earning under $37,000, affecting 2.1 million women, delays the super guarantee rise to 12 per cent at a cost of $53 billion in national savings by 2021 to 2022, and cuts the schoolkids bonus of $410 and $820 per student for 1.3 million families.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Opposed repealing the mining tax, warning the abolition of the Regional Infrastructure Fund leaves many projects with no confirmed funding, and quoted a 2011 speech criticising mining companies for investing little back into the communities whose resources they extract, before revealing the quote came from the now Deputy Prime Minister.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the mining tax, criticising the Regional Development Australia Fund for committing $916 million, or 95 per cent, of its $952 million allocation by election time, including $608 million in the final three and a half months, and said Australia had accumulated $300 billion in debt in six years under the previous government.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Opposed repealing the mining tax, defending the schoolkids bonus of $410 and $820 per student for 1.3 million families, criticising the delay to raising the super guarantee from nine to 12 per cent, and citing estimates that scrapping the low-income superannuation contribution would cut national savings by $53 billion by 2021.

speeches.speaker: Brendan O'Connor
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, arguing that repealing the minerals resource rent tax would remove the schoolkids bonus, low-income superannuation support, the income support bonus and small-business tax concessions, while increasing taxes on low-paid workers and reducing investment in infrastructure.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, arguing that repealing the minerals resource rent tax would improve the budget bottom line by $15 billion over the current forward estimates, restore investor confidence, reduce compliance costs and benefit Western Australia's mining and regional sectors.

speeches.speaker: Pat Conroy
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, arguing that the minerals resource rent tax fairly shared mining superprofits with Australians and funded support for families, low-income workers, small businesses and mining-affected regions, while its repeal would benefit large mining companies at others' expense.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Argued that mineral resources belong to the states, supporting the principle underlying state royalty provisions.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, arguing that it would benefit three large multinational mining companies while removing or delaying support for families, small businesses and retirement savings, including the planned increase in compulsory superannuation contributions from nine to 12 per cent.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the minerals resource rent tax, arguing that it was poorly implemented, discouraged foreign investment and harmed growth, jobs and regional Australia, while the coalition was fulfilling its 7 September election mandate.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the Minerals Resource Rent Tax, arguing one company told him it could cost up to $7 million just to collect and remit the tax, more than it delivered in revenue, while conceding a case might exist for retaining a profits-based tax on foreign-owned iron ore or coal miners.

speeches.speaker: Bruce Scott
speeches.brief: Supported repealing the Minerals Resource Rent Tax, citing stalled Queensland coal projects including Waratah Coal's 4,400 million tonne Galilee Basin discovery and Glencore Xstrata's Wandoan project, and said the tax was predicted to raise $26.5 billion over five years but had collected only four hundred million dollars.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Opened his summation of debate on the Minerals Resource Rent Tax repeal bill, criticising the shadow Treasurer's contribution as failing to appreciate the damage caused by the tax and containing several inaccuracies about its operation.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Defended the Minerals Resource Rent Tax Repeal and Other Measures Bill 2013, arguing the government's cuts are necessary because Labor's spending left Australia with more than $400 billion in debt and the five biggest budget deficits in the nation's history.
